blocks.h2: Gas Logs in a Historic Fireplace
blocks.body: Many older Ravenswood homes have small, shallow fireplaces built for burning coal or wood. Not every log set fits safely in a firebox like that, and the chimney has to be in good shape before any gas appliance is used. We help you choose a log set sized for the firebox, run the gas line and valve and test everything. A chimney professional should inspect the flue first.

blocks.h2: What Affects the Price of Fireplace Work
blocks.body: A service visit is simple. A failed part depends on the fireplace. Running gas to an old masonry fireplace depends on the route through the building. We diagnose and quote a flat price.

blocks.h2: Gas Fireplace Questions From Ravenswood Homeowners

items.q: Can my old fireplace be converted to gas?
items.preview: Often, if the chimney is sound.
items.answer: Often. We run the gas line and install the valve. A chimney specialist handles flue work.

items.q: Why won't my pilot stay lit?
items.preview: A dirty pilot or weak thermocouple.
items.answer: Usually a dirty pilot or a weak thermocouple.

items.q: Does the damper stay open with gas logs?
items.answer: Yes. Vented logs need it held partly open.

items.q: When should I service my fireplace?
items.answer: Early fall, before the cold arrives.

items.q: Can a coal-burning fireplace take gas logs?
items.answer: Sometimes. Coal fireplaces are often shallow, so not all log sets fit safely.

items.q: Can you service a gas fireplace in a condo?
items.answer: Yes. We check the valve, pilot and connections.

items.q: How much does gas fireplace repair cost in Ravenswood?
items.preview: It depends on the part. You'll approve a flat price first.
items.answer: It depends on what failed and the type of fireplace. You'll approve a flat-rate price before we start.
